$comment: Files of the v1.8.0 test suite that scripts/run-compat.ts does not run against the current sources. Every entry carries a reason; a behaviour change also names the compatibility-ledger entry (release-notes/v1.9.0.md, Upgrade section) that documents and justifies it. A file listed here without a ledger entry tests the repository tree rather than the engine. Keep this list as short as the ledger: an exclusion that outlives its ledger entry is a hidden breaking change. Exclusions are per file (vitest --exclude); the tests of each file that still hold run in the current suite.

exclude.reason: Repository-tree tests (verify-docs over the site, recipes index, playground inventory, prose language), not engine behaviour — the current suite covers today's tree.

Repository-tree tests (workflow pins, font manifest, generator parity against the committed modules, diagram geometry, agent configuration), not engine behaviour — the current suite covers today's tree.

Reads the sample PDFs the 1.8.0 generators wrote into test-output/ and the 1.8.0 byte manifest; the current suite holds the current generators to the current chain, whose carried-forward entries are the 1.8.0 bytes.
Pins the exact list of registered shapers (twelve in 1.8.0); five Indic scripts were added in 1.9.0, an inventory change the current suite pins at seventeen — no 1.8.0 shaper moved or left.

Three 1.8.0 golden tests assert that the first glyph of a split vowel sign (Tamil கொ, Bengali কো, Sinhala කො) reports the precomposed code point and the second part none; since 1.9.0 each part names its code point of the canonical decomposition so every glyph is in /ToUnicode and level U never finds a glyph without a Unicode value (the extracted NFD text normalises back to the source). The current suite holds every other assertion of the file to the same glyph sequences.

Compares glyph positions and rendered pixels with the 1.8.0 baselines; mark anchors (Tibetan, Khmer, Myanmar, USE), per-paragraph BiDi and the lean subsets move them on purpose, and the regenerated baselines are reviewed in the current suite.

Three tests pin the pre-1.9.0 lite algorithm: General Punctuation and whitespace classes that UAX #9 assigns differently (U+2030/U+2032 are ET, TAB is S), and brackets inside an LTR run of an RTL paragraph that N0 now pairs and L4 mirrors. The full UAX #9 resolver passes BidiCharacterTest.

Three tests pin the 1.3.0 'lite forcing' of LRO/RLO overrides (inner controls stripped, Arabic kept in logical order); X1–X8 now resolve overrides as the standard does, with the override's level and direction.

Six tests pin the 1.4.0 isolate handling (isolates re-resolved as separate segments, unmatched PDI/LRI dropped); BD9 matching and X5a–X6a now give isolates their own level inside the paragraph's resolution.

One test pins the 1.8.0 ToUnicode rule 'the smallest code point of the cmap wins'; the encoded code point now has priority over the inverted cmap, so shaper-produced glyphs are named with the text they came from.
Two tests pin the decomposed extraction of Thai and Lao sara am in untagged documents; the untagged path now writes /Span /ActualText per cluster, so extraction restores U+0E33 and U+0EB3 as typed.
Two tests pin the degraded base-14 rendering of U+202F (narrow no-break space) as an ordinary space; the Latin path now emits a TJ adjustment that keeps its width and extraction.
Two tests pin the single refusal of layout.pdfx with any layout.tagged; the joint PDF/A-2b/2u + PDF/X-4 claim is allowed, and the refusal is now one message per excluded level (1b, 3b).

Six tests compare scanDeviceColour's result with toEqual; the result gained the `named` list (the /Separation and /DeviceN names a content stream selects) so spot-colour resources can be written. An added field, every 1.8.0 field unchanged.

Three tests pin one `BT … ET` text object per shaped glyph (txtShaped) and one per run of a multi-font line; a line is one text object now, a shaped run one TJ array, so a /ActualText span never wraps more than one text object and Acrobat pastes a cell's text once instead of once per glyph. Every other assertion of the file holds in the current suite.

Three tests look for presentation-form glyph ids in the content stream and one expects a bracketed Latin island to extract as one piece of a visual-order line; glyph codes are the document's CIDs now (C28) and every right-to-left run carries its logical text as /ActualText, each bracket with its own run (C27). The current suite holds the same joining and extraction facts through the encoding context and the spans.

Five tests read source glyph ids out of textRuns() and ps() hex strings (the space as <0003>, Thai ก as <000A>, Hebrew mem-final as <0021>); the hex strings carry CIDs allotted in order of first use since C28, and the current suite asserts the same facts through getCidMaps().

Thirteen tests look glyph codes up in the font module's widths and outlines and call applyFeaturesToRuns() on CID-coded runs without the code → glyph resolver the wrappers take since C28; the current suite checks the same embedding, width and outline facts against the compact subset.

One test calls applyKerningToRuns() on CID-coded runs without the code → glyph resolver (C28); kerning through the context (layout.typography.kerning) is held by the rest of the file and the current suite.
One test sums a justified line's advances by looking its hex codes up in the font module's widths; the codes are CIDs since C28 and the current suite resolves them through getCidMaps().
